topic: Counselling a woman with recurrent miscarriage
scenario: You are the house officer in the gynaecology clinic. Mrs Perera is 31 and has had three consecutive first-trimester miscarriages. She has come with her husband to discuss why this has happened and what can be done. Her investigations are not yet back.

questions.prompt: Explain to the couple what recurrent miscarriage means and how common it is.
marking_points: Defines recurrent miscarriage as three or more consecutive losses before 24 weeks
States it affects about 1% of couples
Explains that most couples go on to have a successful pregnancy

questions.prompt: Describe the investigations you would arrange and why.
marking_points: Antiphospholipid antibodies — lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin, repeated 12 weeks apart
Parental karyotyping where a fetal loss is found to be unbalanced
Thyroid function and HbA1c where clinically indicated
Explains that no cause is found in about half of couples
Checks the couple's understanding before moving on

questions.prompt: Outline the management if antiphospholipid syndrome is confirmed.
marking_points: Low-dose aspirin from a positive pregnancy test
Low molecular weight heparin once a fetal heart is seen
States this improves the live birth rate substantially
Arranges early pregnancy unit referral and supportive care
